evals.prompt:
Write a PR description for the following changes. This is a refactoring PR.

Commit log:
- refactor: extract shared validation into middleware
- refactor: consolidate error response helpers
- refactor: remove duplicate config parsing

Diff summary:
- New file: middleware/validation.go — moved validateRequestBody, validatePagination, validateUUID from 4 handler files
- New file: errors/responses.go — moved respondError, respondNotFound, respondForbidden from 6 handler files
- Deleted: helpers_test.go (tests moved to middleware/validation_test.go)
- Modified: all handler files to use new middleware and error helpers
- Modified: router.go to register validation middleware
- Modified: go.sum (no new dependencies)

Context: This is a Go REST API. The previous PR (#15) added 6 new endpoints, which introduced the duplication that this PR cleans up. The API serves a task management app.
evals.expected_output: PR description with Summary-only narrative explaining why this refactoring is happening now (after PR #15), including judgment on why each consolidation was needed
assertions: Summary is written as prose paragraphs, not a bullet list
Summary mentions PR #15 or the prior PR as project context for why this refactoring is happening now
Summary does not contain function names (validateRequestBody, validatePagination, etc.) or file names (validation.go, responses.go)
Summary includes judgment on why the changes were needed, not just what was done
No em dashes in the output
Test plan is omitted (pure refactoring with existing test coverage)

evals.prompt:
Write a PR description for the following changes. This is a new feature PR.

Commit log:
- feat: add WebSocket server for real-time notifications
- feat: add notification persistence layer
- feat: add client subscription management

Diff summary:
- New file: ws/server.go — WebSocket upgrade handler, connection pool, broadcast
- New file: ws/subscription.go — per-user topic subscriptions, unsubscribe on disconnect
- New file: store/notifications.go — PostgreSQL-backed notification storage with read/unread status
- New file: store/notifications_test.go — integration tests
- Modified: router.go — added /ws endpoint
- Modified: docker-compose.yml — no changes to services, only added test env vars
- Modified: go.mod, go.sum — added gorilla/websocket v1.5.3

Context: The app is a collaborative document editor. Users have been requesting real-time notifications for comments and mentions. Currently notifications are polled every 30 seconds via REST, causing unnecessary load and delayed feedback. The team decided on WebSockets over SSE because the app will need bidirectional communication for live cursors in a future PR.
evals.expected_output: PR description with Summary explaining the user problem (polling delay + load), why WebSockets over SSE, and what was introduced
assertions: Summary is written as prose paragraphs, not a bullet list
Summary explains the user-facing problem (polling delay, unnecessary load)
Summary mentions the WebSocket vs SSE decision and the reason (bidirectional communication for future live cursors)
Summary does not contain file names (server.go, subscription.go, notifications.go)
No em dashes in the output
Summary uses paragraph breaks to separate context from approach

evals.prompt:
Write a PR description for the following changes. This is a bug fix PR.

Related issue: #42 — 'Cursor pagination returns duplicate items when records share the same created_at timestamp'

Commit log:
- fix: add UUID tie-breaker to cursor pagination
- test: add regression test for duplicate-timestamp pagination

Diff summary:
- Modified: pagination.go — cursor now encodes (created_at, uuid) instead of just created_at; query uses (created_at, uuid) > ($1, $2) instead of created_at > $1
- Modified: pagination_test.go — added TestPaginationDuplicateTimestamp that inserts 5 records with same timestamp and verifies no duplicates across 3 pages
- Modified: topic_handler.go, session_handler.go, message_handler.go — updated cursor construction to include UUID

Context: A user reported seeing the same topic appear on consecutive pages. Investigation revealed that when multiple records share a created_at timestamp, the old cursor (timestamp-only) couldn't distinguish them, causing the DB to return overlapping results.
evals.expected_output: PR description with Summary explaining the bug, root cause, and fix approach with judgment on why UUID tie-breaker was chosen
assertions: Summary is written as prose paragraphs, not a bullet list
Summary references issue #42 or describes the user-reported bug (duplicate items on consecutive pages)
Summary explains the root cause (timestamp-only cursor cannot distinguish records with same created_at)
Summary explains the fix approach and why it was chosen
Summary does not list individual modified files (pagination.go, topic_handler.go, etc.)
No em dashes in the output

evals.prompt:
Write a PR description for the following changes. This is a tool introduction PR.

Commit log:
- feat: add textlint for Japanese technical writing
- fix: resolve textlint warnings in existing docs
- chore: add textlint to pre-commit hook and CI

Diff summary:
- New file: .textlintrc.json — configuration with preset-ja-technical-writing and preset-jtf-style, sentence-length rule disabled
- New file: .github/workflows/textlint.yml — CI workflow running textlint on docs/**/*.md
- Modified: package.json — added textlint, textlint-rule-preset-ja-technical-writing, textlint-rule-preset-jtf-style as devDependencies
- Modified: .husky/pre-commit — added npx textlint command
- Modified: 24 files in docs/ — fixed redundant expressions, terminology inconsistencies, and sentence length issues detected by textlint

Context: This is a documentation-heavy repository for a developer portal. Documentation reviews repeatedly flagged the same writing issues — redundant expressions (e.g., 「することができる」), inconsistent terminology, and overly long sentences. The team chose textlint over alternatives like RedPen because textlint has a richer ecosystem of Japanese-specific presets and runs on the existing Node.js toolchain (ESLint and Prettier are already in use). The sentence-length rule was disabled because existing docs frequently exceed the default limit and fixing all of them was out of scope for this PR.
evals.expected_output: PR description with Summary explaining the repeated review problem, why textlint was chosen, and configuration judgment. No Changes section, no Test plan
assertions: Summary is written as prose paragraphs, not a bullet list
Summary explains why automated linting is needed (repeated review feedback on writing issues)
Summary mentions the tool selection rationale (textlint chosen over alternatives, Japanese presets, Node.js toolchain)
Summary includes a link to textlint or describes it in a way a reviewer unfamiliar with the tool can understand
Summary explains configuration judgment (e.g., why sentence-length rule was disabled)
Summary does not contain file counts (24 files) or file names (.textlintrc.json)
No em dashes in the output
Test plan section is omitted (documentation and config changes only)
